Volley Manager arose from the real need to organize volleyball matches fairly and dynamically. Who has never experienced the problem of unbalanced teams or confusion when knowing who is next to play? The app takes care of the queue, skill level (through Elo) and everyone\'s fun. If you have any suggestions or found a problem, do not hesitate to use the button below to send your feedback!

Open-source project developed natively in Kotlin with Jetpack Compose. The architecture follows the clean MVVM pattern, using Room Database for local and offline storage of all data. To delve into the architecture or contribute to the project, access the documentation via the button below.

Hello! I am Bruno Bismarck, developer and UX Designer behind this project. I created this application with dedication to make life easier for those who organize games with friends. Follow my work, say hello and stay up to date with the news through my Instagram by clicking the button below!

How to create or manage groups?

In the side menu, you can create different \"Groups\". This is useful if you play in different places or with different classes (eg Saturday Volleyball and Company Volleyball). Each group has its own history and list of players.

Recreational: two teams of 2 to 6 players, no fixed positions. Balancing uses Elo and the priority flag. Fixed Positions: two teams of 2 to 7 players; each player registers a preferred and a second position, and teams respect the minimum composition for that team size. Tournament modes (recreational and pro) already exist in the app but are not available to choose yet.
How does the app choose who plays the next match?

In Recreational groups, the app picks the top players from the queue, ordered in alternating skill levels, to create Elo-balanced teams (respecting the Priority flag when it\'s enabled). In Fixed Positions groups, the queue order is also respected, but each required slot is filled starting from the most restrictive position, balancing Elo among the players who fit each slot. In both cases, you can reorder the queue or make substitutions manually, if needed.
What is the difference between balancing modes?

Rebalance Mode splits the winning team into two and fills them with players from the top of the queue to keep skill levels balanced. Rest Mode forces the winning team to rest for one round if there are two or more full teams in the queue; otherwise, the winners keep playing. Both modes are available in Recreational and Fixed Positions groups (tournament types don\'t use them).
What happens when the victory limit is reached?

When a team reaches the set limit, they become \'King of the Court\' and will either split, rest, or keep playing, depending on the balancing mode and queue size. When the team is split, it\'s divided into two Elo-balanced halves and each half is completed with players from the queue.
How do substitutions work during a match?

Just long-press the person you want to remove, tap who\'s replacing them, and confirm. You can substitute court players with those in the waiting line or in the bench, as well as swap players between the two teams on the court.
When should I use manual team setup?
Use this only for unusual situations, like when a match is already in progress when you open the app. Overall, automatic mode is faster and more consistent.
What do the Elo change values mean on the History screen?

Visible when the \"Show Elo\" option is enabled, these values show the match\'s impact on Elo. Values close to 16 indicate well-balanced teams. Well below 16 usually means the favored team won. Above 16 indicates a victory by a team with a lower average Elo (an upset).

Available only in Recreational-type groups (Fixed Positions groups use the position composition and the \"Guarantee a setter\" option instead). It serves to ensure that certain positions or skill levels are well distributed. For example, if you mark the setters with \"Priority\", the app will try to place a setter on each side when generating teams automatically.
What do the position abbreviations mean in Fixed Positions mode?
Which positions and roles make up each team size in Fixed Positions mode?

2x2|With "Guarantee a setter": 1 setter + 1 player in any other position (outside hitter, opposite, middle blocker or libero). Without it: 1st slot is attack (setter, outside hitter or opposite) + 1 defense (middle blocker or libero).
3x3|1st slot follows the setter rule + 1 attacker (outside hitter or opposite) + 1 defender (middle blocker or libero).
4x4|1st slot follows the setter rule + 1 attacker (outside hitter or opposite) + 2 defenders (max 1 outside hitter on defense).
5x5|1st slot follows the setter rule + 2 attackers (outside hitters or opposites) + 2 defenders (max 1 outside hitter on defense).
6x6|Setter, attacking outside hitter, defending outside hitter, 1st middle blocker, opposite and libero (or a 2nd middle blocker if there is no libero).
7x7|Same base as 6x6 plus 1 extra middle blocker; the libero stays on the bench and can swap with any middle blocker on the team.
What is the role of each position in Fixed Positions mode?

Setter|Team playmaker/strategist. In 2x2 to 5x5, if the guarantee is off and no setter is available, the slot can be filled by an attacker.
Outside Hitter|Attack and defense: with 1 on the team, counts as attack; with 2, one becomes the attacking outside hitter and the other the defending one.
Opposite|Counts as attack.
Middle Blocker|Counts as defense.
Libero|Counts as defense.

When activated, it shows each player\'s number of matches. If a player arrives late, the average number of matches the group had already played up to their arrival is added, so latecomers don\'t jump ahead of those who have been waiting since the start. Players who arrive together with the group start with zero extra matches.

Elo is a scoring system that evaluates the skill level of each player. You earn points when you win and lose when you are defeated, based on the difficulty of the match. The average Elo is simply the sum of a team\'s points divided by the number of players.

Last update: April 2026

Volley Manager is a free, open-source application for organizing recreational volleyball matches.

1. Collected data
The application exclusively stores the data you provide manually: player names, groups, match history, and Elo ratings. No sensitive personal data (e-mail, phone, location, device identifiers) is collected.

2. Local storage
All data is stored locally on your device, using the application's internal database (Room/SQLite). No data is sent to external servers.

3. Data sharing
The application does not share data with third parties. Export functions (CSV/JSON) and result image sharing are actions initiated exclusively by you.

4. Third-party services
The application does not use analytics, tracking, advertising, or any other service that collects user data.

5. Permissions
The application does not request special device permissions other than those necessary for reading/writing files, in case you use the export/import function.

6. Data deletion
You can delete any data at any time directly through the application (delete players, clear history) or by uninstalling the application, which removes all stored data.

7. Children
The application is not directed at children under 13 and does not knowingly collect data from children.

8. Contact
Questions about this policy can be sent to the developer through the application page on the Google Play Store.
